column1: Classify and manage repositories or datasets containing personal data by considering the potential adverse impact (e.g. reputational or financial) to the individuals involved should the data be compromised.

column1: Conduct data protection impact assessment (' DPIA ') before development to assess the types of personal data and the data processing activities required for achieving the purposes of a new ICT system.

column1: Conduct periodic checks for personal data stored in ICT systems. For personal data that is not required in any form anymore, securely dispose of the data. If there is a need to retain the data but in anonymised or aggregated form, e.g. for performing data analytics, consider anonymising the data.
column2: Conduct periodic checks for personal data stored in ICT systems. For personal data that is not required in any form anymore, securely dispose of the data. column1: Conduct physical asset inventory checks regularly to ensure that all computers and other electronic devices (e.g. portable hard drives, printers, fax machines) used to store or process personal data are accounted for.
column2: Conduct physical asset inventory checks regularly to ensure that all computers and other electronic devices (e.g. portable hard drives, printers, fax machines) used to store or process personal data are accounted for.

column1: Do not collect personal data unless it will be used and there is valid purpose for doing it. Trace every data element that you are collecting to identify which internal department uses it,how it is used and whether it is necessary.
column2: Do not collect personal data unless it will be used and there is valid purpose for doing it. Trace every data element that you are collecting to identify which internal department uses it,how it is used and whether it is necessary.

column1: When different types of personal data can be used to achieve the same purpose, collect the least sensitive types of personal data (e.g. collect approximate location data of users rather than their exact locations).
column2: When different types of personal data can be used to achieve the same purpose, collect the least sensitive types of personal data (e.g. collect approximate location data of users rather than their exact locations).

column1: Personal data may be inadvertently collected in the form of metadata (e.g. EXIF data in image files). Consider not collecting such data or removing them if they are not needed.
